findings.highlight: without his master
findings.evidenceJa: [ruby text=あるじ char=2]遠坂の下を離れて
findings.governingReading: having left Tohsaka—read as his master—behind
findings.explanation: The English preserves the ruby relation but removes Rin’s identity from Archer’s departure.

findings.highlight: states the question I must answer
findings.evidenceJa: 俺が出すべき答えをカタチにした
findings.governingReading: Archer gives form, more clearly than Shirou can, to the answer Shirou must give.
findings.explanation: The English reverses answer into question and weakens Archer’s role as embodying the demanded conclusion.

findings.highlight: If you equate self-imprisonment with death
findings.evidenceJa: 自らを閉ざす事を死というのならば
findings.governingReading: If closing oneself off counts as death.
findings.explanation: The English makes existential self-closure sound like literal confinement.

findings.highlight: the crime will definitely judge you
findings.evidenceJa: その[ruby text=つけ]罪は必ず、おまえ自身を裁くだろう
findings.governingReading: That sin—read as the reckoning or price due—will surely judge you yourself.
findings.explanation: The ruby’s debt or reckoning force disappears, and the emphatic judgment of Shirou by his own choice is flattened.

findings.highlight: Its location suits an indecisive guy like me
findings.evidenceJa: 中途半端な場所だった
findings.governingReading: It was a halfway, neither-here-nor-there place suited to someone unable to decide anything.
findings.explanation: The English omits the spatial and moral “halfway” correspondence central to the park’s location.

findings.highlight: She has suffered sexual abuse
findings.evidenceJa: 間桐の後継者として、実験台にされ続けてきた
findings.governingReading: As the Matou successor, she has continually been used as an experimental subject.
findings.explanation: The mature branch deletes Sakura’s heir status and prolonged magical experimentation, replacing them with a narrower categorical claim.

findings.highlight: a woman who has known men
findings.evidenceJa: 蟲に汚された[ruby text=あま char=2]魔女
findings.governingReading: a witch tainted by worms
findings.explanation: The mature branch replaces the Matou worm violation and witch condemnation with sexual experience involving unspecified men.

findings.highlight: it can’t even drown out the hatred
findings.evidenceJa: 憎悪を切り裂く事もできやしない
findings.governingReading: The direct nerve pain cannot even cut through the hatred in his head.
findings.explanation: The English replaces the image of pain cutting hatred with suppression by drowning it out.

findings.highlight: I accepted her as a matter of course
findings.evidenceJa: 俺は当然のように甘受していた
findings.governingReading: Without knowing the pain supporting Sakura’s gentle smile, Shirou had accepted and enjoyed that smile as though it were simply due.
findings.explanation: The object shifts from the comfort Sakura’s smiles gave Shirou to Sakura herself, erasing his recognition of taking her care for granted.

findings.highlight: It makes me want to kill him
findings.evidenceJa: 殺したくなる
findings.governingReading: It makes Shirou want to kill; the target is disclosed by the following outcry.
findings.explanation: The English supplies a male target before the Japanese reveals whom Shirou means.

findings.highlight: Shinji wouldn’t have lost himself
findings.evidenceJa: 今まで通りにやっていけた
findings.governingReading: Shinji would not have become so distraught and they could have carried on as before.
findings.explanation: The English intensifies Shinji’s loss of composure into losing himself and omits the imagined continuation of ordinary life.

findings.highlight: The clear colors transfer into my head
findings.evidenceJa: 鮮やかな色彩に意識が移って
findings.governingReading: His attention shifts to the vivid color.
findings.explanation: The English reverses what moves and produces an unnatural claim that colors enter Shirou’s head.

findings.highlight: It makes me jealous, as if something important has been taken away
findings.evidenceJa: ちろりと動く蛇の舌のように、大事にしていたモノを奪われた嫉妬が走る
findings.governingReading: Jealousy at having something precious taken from him darts through him like a flickering snake’s tongue.
findings.explanation: The English removes the sharp, intrusive snake-tongue image and weakens the possession as hypothetical.

findings.highlight: it’s my fault
findings.evidenceJa: 俺だけの落ち度だ
findings.governingReading: It is Shirou’s failing alone.
findings.explanation: The English omits Shirou’s insistence on exclusive personal responsibility.

findings.highlight: I believed him
findings.evidenceJa: 俺はそれを信じきった
findings.governingReading: Shirou believed Zouken completely.
findings.explanation: The English drops the totality of Shirou’s credulity, which drives his self-indictment.

findings.highlight: I believed his words
findings.evidenceJa: 簡単に鵜呑みにした
findings.governingReading: He readily swallowed Zouken’s words whole because they suited him.
findings.explanation: The English removes Shirou’s accusation that his acceptance was easy and uncritical.

findings.highlight:
she’s been
 raped
findings.evidenceJa: 決して口に出せない境遇に耐えていた
findings.governingReading: she had endured circumstances she could never bring herself to speak of
findings.explanation: The mature branch replaces deliberately bounded knowledge about Sakura’s unspeakable circumstances with an explicit factual claim of rape at this point.

findings.highlight: fight against him
findings.evidenceJa: その者達と戦わなくてはならなくなる
findings.governingReading: A champion of justice must fight such people—those who are evil to others.
findings.explanation: The English narrows Shirou’s general rule back to Zouken alone, weakening the rule that will also condemn Sakura.

findings.highlight: use Rider to indiscriminately attack people
findings.evidenceJa: 見境なしにライダーを使役する
findings.governingReading: deploy Rider indiscriminately, as Sakura just did
findings.explanation: The English specifies attacks on people rather than Sakura’s loss of discrimination in commanding Rider.

findings.highlight: I’ve been able to live because I have to save people
findings.evidenceJa: 人々を救うからと、こうして生きていられた
findings.governingReading: He has been able to go on living on the premise that he will save people from senseless calamity.
findings.explanation: The English turns the ideal that sustains Shirou’s life into an external obligation.

findings.highlight: I had to greet you
findings.evidenceJa: つい声かけちゃった
findings.governingReading: Illya happened to call out to Shirou when she spotted him while walking through town.
findings.explanation: Spontaneous, delighted impulse becomes necessity, and her walk through town disappears.

findings.highlight: It looks like she knows about Sakura’s condition
findings.evidenceJa: 桜の容体を笑っているように見えて
findings.governingReading: To Shirou, Illya appears to be laughing at Sakura’s condition.
findings.explanation: The English replaces Shirou’s hostile misreading of Illya’s cheerful manner with the neutral fact that she seems informed.

findings.highlight: an honest, pure show of affection
findings.evidenceJa: 裏表のない純粋な好意
findings.governingReading: Illya’s straightforward, guileless affection itself
findings.explanation: The English externalizes Illya’s feeling as a display or gesture, weakening the sincerity Shirou recognizes.

findings.highlight: that phrase washes everything away from my head
findings.evidenceJa: ガツンと、頭の中をキレイさっぱり洗われた
findings.governingReading: The single statement hits Shirou hard and washes his mind completely clean.
findings.explanation: The English removes both the forceful impact and the completeness of the mental reset.

findings.highlight: protect the ones you love
findings.evidenceJa: 好きな子のことを守る
findings.governingReading: protect the person you love or like
findings.explanation: Illya’s pointed singular principle, directly applicable to Sakura, becomes a generalized plural maxim.
